title: Zhang Qian's Thirteen-Year Mission
text:
Around 138 BC Emperor Wu of Han wanted allies against the Xiongnu, the nomadic empire that raided China's northern frontier. He had heard that a people called the Yuezhi, driven west by the Xiongnu, wanted revenge. He asked for volunteers to find them. Zhang Qian, a palace official, set out with more than a hundred men and a guide named Ganfu.

Sima Qian records what happened. Crossing Xiongnu territory, Zhang Qian was captured. He was held for more than ten years and given a Xiongnu wife, with whom he had a son. But he kept the staff that marked him as the Han emperor's envoy, and finally he escaped and continued west.

He passed through Dayuan, in the Ferghana valley, and Kangju, and found the Yuezhi settled in rich lands near Bactria. They no longer wanted war with the Xiongnu. His mission had failed. On the way home he was captured by the Xiongnu again, and held for more than a year before escaping in a time of turmoil.

In 126 BC he reached China with only Ganfu of the original party. His reports on the kingdoms, horses and trade routes of Central Asia led to Han expansion westward and the opening of the routes later called the Silk Road.
lesson: Stay loyal to your purpose through setbacks you cannot control. Even a mission that fails at its first goal can change the world through what you bring back.
people: Zhang Qian, Emperor Wu of Han, Ganfu
location: From Chang'an (modern Xi'an, China) to Central Asia
source: Sima Qian, Shiji (Records of the Grand Historian), chapter 123; Ban Gu, Han Shu, chapter 61
